critical_issues.description: Hardcoded string 'dashboard' and 'flood' in assertion may cause false negatives if content is localized, transpiled, or minified; should use more robust pattern matching or be aligned with actual frontend implementation.

Assertion 'fetch(' in content.replace(" ", "")' is redundant and inefficient; the same check is performed twice with and without spaces, but the second check is logically identical to the first due to incorrect use of replace.
Module-level assert statement will cause test suite to fail on import if router is not a FastAPI instance, violating pytest best practices and preventing test discovery.
Test for /items endpoint assumes get_items returns a list, but API contract does not specify response schema for /items; mismatch between test assumptions and documented contracts.
Test for POST /items assumes 201 status, but API contract does not specify status code for item creation; test may pass while implementation is non-compliant.

File extension '.py' is misleading for a JavaScript test file; the file contains JavaScript tests but is named as Python, which may cause confusion in CI/CD and tooling (e.g., linters, formatters, test runners).
Test `test_app_js_contains_expected_api_endpoints` duplicates logic in `test_app_js_contains_fetch_calls_with_expected_paths`, increasing maintenance burden and risk of inconsistent assertions.
Missing import for pytest; while pytest is used implicitly via assert, the test file should explicitly import pytest for clarity and to avoid potential runtime issues in some environments.

Module-level instantiation of TestClient(app) may cause issues in concurrent test runs or when app state is mutated between tests. The client should be provided via a fixture (e.g., using @pytest.fixture) to ensure proper isolation and lifecycle management.

The test does not validate the exact value of 'status' field beyond type; per API contract, it should be 'healthy' or similar expected value. A more robust assertion is needed to ensure the response matches the documented contract.

File name 'test_static_css_style.css.py' is misleading and non-standard: pytest expects test files to end with 'test_*.py' or '*_test.py', and this name suggests it's a CSS file masquerading as a Python test file, which violates naming conventions and may cause test discovery issues.
Test uses '/health' endpoint, but API contract specifies '/api/v1/health'. This mismatch will cause test to fail or test incorrect behavior.

Test expects response body {'status': 'healthy'}, but API contract only specifies 'status' as a string without value constraints. Should verify actual response value matches implementation, but more importantly, the endpoint path is wrong.

Module-level mutation of app (app.include_router(router)) causes side effects during import, which violates test isolation and can lead to unpredictable behavior when tests run in parallel or when modules are imported multiple times.
Test functions directly use a global app instance instead of creating a fresh app per test, risking state leakage between tests.

Missing import for 'Path' from 'pathlib' is already present, but the code uses 'Path(__file__)' without ensuring 'Path' is imported correctly — however, the import is correct. The real critical issue is the missing '/api/v1/health' endpoint as required by the API contracts.
Missing '/api/v1/health' endpoint that must return {"status": "..."} per API contract; current implementation has no health check endpoint.
Missing import for FastAPI's Depends and status codes (e.g., HTTP_200_OK, HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST); also missing uvicorn, but more critically, missing proper error handling imports.
SensorData model uses datetime without timezone awareness; this can cause inconsistent storage and comparison issues across timezones.
get_sensor_data() returns raw database rows as dicts without validation against SensorData model, risking malformed or malicious data exposure.
add_sensor_data() does not validate or sanitize input before DB insertion; timestamp.isoformat() may fail if timezone info is missing or malformed.
get_inundation_map() is incomplete (truncated at line 95), missing return statement and exception handling cleanup.
Missing API health endpoint '/api/v1/health' as required by API contracts.
The 'status-loading' element contains placeholder text ('Loading system status...') instead of meaningful, real-time status labels as required by the design checklist.
The 'data-loading' element contains placeholder text ('Fetching real-time sensor data...') instead of meaningful, real-time data labels.
The 'action-loading' element contains placeholder text ('Initializing evacuation routing engine...') instead of meaningful, real-time status labels.
The error section uses 'style="display: none;"' inline instead of a CSS class for state management, violating CSS variable and maintainability requirements.
CSS file is incomplete - '.text-center' class definition is cut off mid-declaration, causing parsing failure and breaking all subsequent styles.
File begins with invalid syntax: triple-quoted string literal (Python-style) instead of JavaScript comment or code. This will cause immediate parse failure in browsers.
Invalid escape sequence '\n' in string literal context (after closing quotes), indicating malformed file structure or copy-paste artifact.
Missing semicolon after string literal and invalid continuation of code (DOM object definition starts without proper JS syntax).
DOM object contains no initialization logic, no DOMContentLoaded handler, and no actual DOM element assignments (all values are null). This will cause runtime errors when DOM elements are accessed.
File is truncated mid-identifier (evacuationMapProgressLoadS...), indicating incomplete or corrupted file content. Critical functionality is missing.

moderate_issues.description: Path construction uses string literal 'static' instead of configurable or environment-aware path; should use environment variable or configuration to support different deployment contexts.
File is opened without context manager safety for read operations; while 'with' is used, no error handling for file I/O (e.g., PermissionError, UnicodeDecodeError) is present.
CSS variable checks are case-sensitive and brittle; production CSS may use different casing or formatting (e.g., minified), and no validation of variable usage beyond presence is performed.
Using MagicMock() without specifying return_value or side_effect may lead to tests that pass incorrectly; consider using spec or spec_set to enforce interface compliance.
Same as above — mock_redis should use spec or spec_set to match actual Redis client interface for more realistic testing.
test_router_exists is redundant and adds no value; router is already validated in module-level code (though that should be removed).
Error message assertion in 404 test is fragile: checking for 'not found' in lowercase or exact string 'Item not found' may break if error message format changes.
Validation error test does not assert response body structure beyond status code; should verify error format matches FastAPI's default validation error schema.

The health endpoint test assumes the response body is exactly {'status': 'healthy'}, but the API contract only specifies 'status' as a string. This may be too strict if the backend returns additional fields (e.g., {'status': 'healthy', 'version': '1.0'}).

The static files test checks for a specific string in the HTML body ('real-time-urban-flood-inundation-mapping'), which couples tests too tightly to implementation details (e.g., page title or meta tags). This makes tests brittle to content changes.
Using `app_js_path.stat().st_size > 0` is fragile; a file could be non-empty but contain only whitespace/comments and still fail functional requirements. Better to validate actual content structure.

The test `test_app_js_contains_fetch_calls_with_expected_paths` only checks for string presence of '/api/v1/health', but does not verify it's used in a valid `fetch()` call (e.g., could be in a comment or string literal). Should assert structural correctness.

The regex-free pattern matching in `test_app_js_exports_or_defines_expected_functions` is overly permissive and may pass for invalid JS (e.g., 'const' in a comment). Should use a proper JS parser or stricter regex.

The test for dashboard page only checks for static asset paths as substrings in HTML, which is brittle and does not guarantee the assets are actually loaded or functional. A more robust approach would be to verify the presence of correct <link> and <script> tags with proper attributes.

The test for /static/index.html does not verify the content type (e.g., 'text/html') or check for expected HTML structure, which could mask issues like misconfigured static file serving or incorrect MIME types.

The assertion 'var(' in content' is insufficient to confirm CSS variable usage; it could match false positives (e.g., in comments or strings). A more robust check would parse CSS or use regex to detect actual var() usage in property values.
Checking for presence of 'color', 'font-size', etc. as substrings is overly simplistic and may yield false positives (e.g., in comments or strings). A proper CSS parser would be more reliable.

Basic brace/parentheses balancing is insufficient for CSS syntax validation; malformed but balanced CSS (e.g., invalid selectors, missing semicolons) would pass. Consider using a real CSS parser like 'cssutils' or 'tinycss2'.
Fixture returns a Path but no guarantee the file exists in the test environment; tests should be isolated and not depend on external filesystem state. Consider mocking or using temporary directories.

Patch is applied to 'src.main.api_router' but the patching context doesn't affect the already-instantiated app; the patch is ineffective for verifying router inclusion since app.routes is already populated at import time.

test_docs_endpoint_exists checks for 'swagger-ui' or 'redoc' in response text, but FastAPI may render either; better to assert status code and presence of expected HTML elements or use schema validation.
test_openapi_schema_exists does not verify that the documented '/api/v1/health' endpoint is present in the schema, despite being the only documented endpoint.
Test data (e.g., location_id, timestamp) uses hardcoded values without context or validation; consider using fixtures or parametrization for better maintainability and clarity.
Missing test for the documented /api/v1/health endpoint, which is referenced in frontend pages and backend checklist.
No validation of response content beyond presence of keys; consider asserting specific value ranges or types for robustness (e.g., inundation_depth_cm should be non-negative).
STATIC_DIR resolution may fail if parent directory does not exist or is not accessible; no validation or fallback for static directory existence.
read_dashboard() returns raw HTML as string or JSON error — inconsistent response type; should return proper HTTP 404 for missing dashboard or use RedirectResponse/HTMLResponse.
No type hints on endpoint functions; production code should include return type annotations (e.g., -> dict, -> str).
DEBUG flag derived directly from ENV without validation; could lead to unsafe production behavior if APP_ENV is set to an unexpected value (e.g., 'prod' vs 'production').
DATABASE_URL default uses sqlite:///app.db, which is inappropriate for production and may cause data loss or security issues if deployed without explicit override.
API_PORT is cast to int without validation; non-numeric port values from environment will raise ValueError at import time.
DB_PATH uses hardcoded fallback 'flood_data.db' without ensuring directory exists; may cause runtime errors on first run.
SensorData.water_level and rainfall use ge=0.0 but do not enforce upper bound; unrealistic values (e.g., 1e9) would pass validation.
InundationMap.status uses regex pattern but does not enforce case-sensitivity; 'Safe' vs 'safe' may cause inconsistencies.
path_coordinates validation only checks min_length=2 but does not validate coordinate structure (e.g., [lon, lat] must be [float, float]).
affected_areas uses min_length=1 but does not enforce uniqueness or non-empty strings in list.
get_db_connection() opens connection without timeout, risking indefinite blocking on concurrent writes.
get_sensor_data() uses SELECT * which may expose unintended columns if schema changes.
add_sensor_data() does not handle duplicate sensor_id entries; may cause unique constraint violations if DB schema enforces uniqueness.
Logger level is set after adding handler, which could cause early log messages to be lost if logger already existed with a different level; better to set level before adding handler.

StreamHandler uses default stderr; for production, consider allowing configurable output stream (e.g., stdout for info/warn, stderr for errors) or using logging.config to support rotation and structured logging.
The 'display' parameter in Google Fonts URL is redundant (implied by 'rel=preconnect' and 'rel=stylesheet') and could cause issues with some CDNs; should be simplified.
The 'aria-busy="true"' attribute is static and never updated by JS, making it misleading; should be dynamically toggled during data loading.
The error section lacks an 'aria-live' attribute, making it inaccessible for screen readers when errors are dynamically displayed.
Color contrast between --color-primary (#1e6f8c) and background (#f8f9fa) may fall below WCAG AA 4.5:1 ratio for normal text; should be verified with contrast checker.
Semantic flood-risk colors duplicate standard semantic colors (e.g., --color-flood-risk-low = --color-success), risking inconsistency if one is updated without the other.
Missing responsive typography scaling (e.g., no media queries or clamp() for base font size), which may cause readability issues on very small or large screens.
Missing responsive container padding (e.g., no reduced padding for mobile viewports), potentially causing horizontal overflow on narrow screens.
API_BASE defined as a string literal without validation or error handling for base URL consistency across environments.
DOM object uses excessive, ungrouped properties (over 50+ entries) without clear organization or documentation, reducing maintainability.
No error handling or null checks for DOM element references before use, risking runtime exceptions.
No fetch/async logic implemented despite API contract requiring GET /api/v1/health; no data fetching or UI update logic present.
No accessibility attributes (aria-labels, roles, keyboard navigation) defined for interactive elements like buttons or maps.

suggestions: Use pytest fixtures or parameterized paths to support configurable static asset directories (e.g., via environment variables or config files).
Add error handling for file operations (e.g., FileNotFoundError, PermissionError) to provide clearer test failure messages.
Replace hardcoded string assertions with more resilient checks (e.g., regex patterns, AST parsing for JS, or semantic validation).
Consider using `pathlib.Path.read_text()` for cleaner file reading instead of manual open/read/close.
Add type hints to function signatures for better IDE and static analysis support.
Normalize whitespace before checking for 'fetch(' to avoid false negatives from inconsistent formatting.
Add tests for other documented API endpoints (e.g., /api/v1/health) to ensure frontend-backend alignment.
Include assertions for accessibility attributes (e.g., aria-labels, semantic HTML) to support the 'accessible' design direction.
Consider adding type hints to fixtures (e.g., -> MagicMock) for better IDE and mypy support.
If actual database or Redis client interfaces are available (e.g., from sqlalchemy.orm.Session or redis.Redis), use spec= or spec_set= to ensure mocks match real APIs.
Add cleanup or reset logic if mocks are mutated during tests to avoid test interdependence.
Document expected behavior of mock_db/mock_redis (e.g., commit(), rollback(), get(), set()) if tests rely on specific methods.
Remove the module-level assert statement and replace with a unit test if router type checking is essential.
Add API contract validation tests that verify response schemas match documented structures (e.g., using pydantic models or jsonschema).
Add tests for missing endpoints (e.g., 404 on unknown paths) to ensure robust error handling.
Use pytest's built-in caplog fixture if logging is involved in route handlers.
Consider parameterizing health endpoint tests to include multiple paths if future extensions are planned.
Add type hints to route handlers in src.api.routes for better maintainability and IDE support.
Ensure all route handlers have proper exception handling for database/network errors not covered in mocks.
Add type hints to test functions (e.g., `def test_main_app_exists() -> None:`) for consistency and IDE support.
Consider parameterizing or mocking the TestClient to avoid repeated instantiation in multiple tests.
Add tests for error cases (e.g., 404 for unknown endpoints, 5xx for server errors) to improve robustness.
Use `response.raise_for_status()` before asserting body/content to catch HTTP errors early.
Verify that the root endpoint (`/`) is intentionally served by the app and not redirected (e.g., to `/dashboard`)—if redirected, adjust the test accordingly.
Rename file to `test_static_js_app.py` to reflect its actual Python implementation.
Replace string-substring checks with AST-based parsing (e.g., using `esprima` via subprocess or `py_mini_racer`) to validate JS structure robustly.
Add a test that verifies `fetch('/api/v1/health')` is called (not just present as text), e.g., using regex like `r'fetch\s*\(\s*["\']\/api\/v1\/health["\']\s*\)'`.
Consider adding a fixture to cache file content to avoid repeated I/O across tests.
Add type hints to fixture and test functions for better IDE/tooling support.
Include a test for error handling (e.g., ensure no hardcoded localhost URLs or debug code in production builds).
Use pytest fixtures (e.g., `@pytest.fixture`) to manage the TestClient instance for better test isolation and reusability.
Add response schema validation using pydantic models or jsonschema to enforce API contract compliance.
Consider using `response.headers.get('content-type')` to assert expected MIME types for HTML and static assets.
Add tests for error cases (e.g., 404, 500) to ensure robust error handling.
Use `assert response.is_success` or `response.status_code == 200` consistently, but prefer explicit status checks for clarity.
Add type hints to test functions and fixtures for better IDE support and documentation.
Rename file to 'test_static_css_style.py' to follow pytest naming conventions.
Add type hints to function signatures (e.g., css_file_path: Path) and fixture return type.
Use pytest's tmp_path fixture or monkeypatch to ensure test isolation instead of relying on filesystem state.
Replace substring checks with regex or a CSS parser (e.g., tinycss2) for more accurate validation.
Add test for CSS file encoding (e.g., UTF-8) to prevent encoding-related issues.
Consider adding a test for CSS file size upper bound to catch accidental inclusion of large assets.
Document the expected CSS structure in test docstrings to improve maintainability.
Update test_health_endpoint to use '/api/v1/health' to match the API contract.
Add test to verify the '/api/v1/health' endpoint returns a response with a 'status' field (e.g., 'healthy', 'ok', etc.) and validate against actual implementation.
Remove ineffective patching in test_app_includes_router; instead, assert on app.routes directly without mocking.
Add tests for error cases (e.g., 404 for unknown endpoints) and ensure type hints are present in source code.
Consider parametrizing or extending openapi schema tests to validate documented endpoints exist in the schema.
Ensure src/main.py does not contain module-level try/except ImportError or self-imports per backend checklist.
Use a pytest fixture to create a fresh app instance per test (e.g., with `@pytest.fixture` and `TestClient(app)` inside the fixture).
Move `app.include_router(router)` inside a fixture or test setup to avoid module-level side effects.
Add tests for error cases beyond 422 (e.g., 400, 500) if applicable.
Consider using `pydantic` models in tests to validate request/response schemas against contracts.
Add type hints to test functions and payloads for better IDE support and documentation.
Add explicit '/api/v1/health' endpoint returning {"status": "healthy"} or similar.
Add error handling for static file serving (e.g., check STATIC_DIR exists before mounting).
Use 'from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse' and return HTMLResponse(index_path.read_bytes()) for better performance and semantics.
Add logging for missing dashboard file instead of silently returning error.
Consider using environment variable or config for static directory path instead of hardcoding relative path.
Add input validation and exception handlers for robustness.
Add OpenAPI tags and descriptions for better API documentation.
Add validation for APP_ENV to ensure it's one of a known set of values (e.g., 'development', 'staging', 'production') before deriving DEBUG.
Remove or replace the default sqlite:///app.db with a more appropriate placeholder (e.g., raise an error if DATABASE_URL is not set).
Validate API_PORT is within valid range (1–65535) and handle invalid values gracefully (e.g., log warning and use default).
Add type hints for all configuration variables (e.g., using typing.Optional and pydantic or dataclasses for stricter validation).
Consider using a configuration validation library (e.g., pydantic-settings) to enforce required env vars and types.
Add comments or docstrings explaining expected environment variable formats (e.g., Redis URL scheme).
Add explicit timezone handling (e.g., use datetime with tzinfo=UTC or convert to ISO 8601 with Z suffix).
Implement Pydantic models for response schemas and use them in endpoint return types.
Add database schema validation/migration tooling (e.g., Alembic) to ensure table existence before queries.
Replace bare `except Exception` with specific exceptions (e.g., sqlite3.Error) and log errors properly.
Add pagination to list endpoints (e.g., /api/sensors) to avoid memory issues with large datasets.
Implement proper input sanitization (e.g., strip whitespace, validate coordinate ranges).
Add database connection pooling or use context managers (`with sqlite3.connect(...) as conn`) for safer resource handling.
Add health endpoint `/api/v1/health` returning `{'status': 'healthy'}`.
Use FastAPI's `Depends` for database connections to enable dependency injection and testing.
Add request/response logging middleware for auditability in production.
Add type hints for handler and formatter objects for better IDE support.
Consider making formatter format string configurable or using dictConfig for production-grade logging configuration.
Add support for environment-based log level override (e.g., LOG_LEVEL env var).
Ensure log messages don't leak sensitive data (e.g., credentials, PII) — though this is application-level, the logger helper should encourage safe patterns.
Add docstring note about thread-safety of handler addition (though logging module handles this, it's good to document).
Replace all placeholder loading text with semantic, real-time status indicators (e.g., 'System operational', 'Data latency: 2s', 'Routing engine ready').
Move the error display state management to CSS classes (e.g., `.error-hidden`) instead of inline styles.
Implement dynamic `aria-busy` toggling in JavaScript during fetch operations.
Add `aria-live="polite"` to the error section for screen reader announcements.
Consider adding a timestamp or last-updated indicator for data freshness transparency.
Ensure `/static/js/app.js` includes error boundary handling and graceful degradation for failed API calls.
Add a `rel="noopener noreferrer"` to external links for security best practices.
Include a skip-to-content link for keyboard accessibility.
Complete the .text-center class definition and ensure all utility classes have full declarations.
Add media queries for responsive breakpoints (e.g., 768px, 1024px) to adjust spacing, font sizes, and container padding.
Implement a dark mode theme using prefers-color-scheme or a toggle mechanism for accessibility.
Add focus-visible polyfill fallback or ensure native :focus-visible support is documented.
Include explicit color-contrast validation in CI/CD pipeline using tools like axe-core or stylelint-config-accessibility.
Consider adding CSS custom properties for font weights (e.g., --font-weight-light, --font-weight-bold) for consistent typography hierarchy.
Add print styles to ensure flood maps and evacuation routes remain usable when printed.
Define explicit z-index scale usage policy to prevent conflicts (e.g., 'never use arbitrary z-index values outside :root').
Replace the invalid Python-style string with a proper JSDoc comment block.
Implement DOMContentLoaded handler to safely initialize DOM references.
Add error boundaries and try/catch blocks around all async API calls.
Refactor DOM object into modular, namespaced objects (e.g., DOM.map, DOM.status).
Implement health check polling with exponential backoff and user-facing error states.
Add responsive viewport meta tag and CSS variables for consistent theming.
Replace placeholder map-related properties with actual canvas rendering logic or map library integration (e.g., Leaflet/Mapbox).
Ensure all interactive elements have visible focus states and keyboard accessibility.
Remove redundant or unused properties (e.g., 30+ event handler placeholders with no implementation).
Add TypeScript types or JSDoc type annotations for improved maintainability.
